instruction:
You are tasked with designing a timer module in Verilog that can be controlled by external signals. The module should have three states: STOP, START, and PAUSE. The timer should start counting seconds when in the START state, pause counting when in the PAUSE state, and reset to zero when in the STOP state. The timer should count at a rate of 25 kHz. The module should have three input signals: clk_i (clock), signal_i (control signal), and a 3-bit signal that corresponds to the buttons on a physical device. The output of the module should be a 32-bit signal that represents the number of seconds that have elapsed since the timer was started.

The control signal should be used to transition between the three states. When the module is in the STOP state, pressing button K3 should transition it to the START state. When the module is in the START state, pressing button K3 should transition it to the PAUSE state, and pressing button K1 should transition it back to the STOP state. When the module is in the PAUSE state, pressing button K3 should transition it back to the START state, and pressing button K1 should transition it back to the STOP state.

You should implement a module called Timer that takes in the following signals:

- clk_i: input clock signal
- signal_i: input control signal
- button_i: input 3-bit signal that corresponds to the buttons on a physical device
- second_o: output 32-bit signal that represents the number of seconds that have elapsed since the timer was started

You should implement the Timer module in no more than 200 lines of Verilog code.
